key_insight: A log‑barrier regularizer combined with a dual‑focused analysis yields the first algorithm that attains the optimal last‑iterate exploitability rate in zero‑sum matrix games under bandit (uncoupled) feedback, matching the known Omega(t^{-1/4)) lower bound.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between lower bounds and prior algorithms by achieving provable last‑iterate convergence (exploitability decay) in zero‑sum matrix games when players receive only bandit feedback and act uncoupled.
method: Use a log‑barrier regularizer inside an online mirror descent framework to prevent boundary collapse and stabilize iterates.
Construct a bandit gradient estimator compatible with the log‑barrier geometry so updates remain unbiased and well‑behaved near simplex boundaries.
Perform a dual‑focused convergence analysis to bound exploitability of the actual iterate and show an O(t^{-1/4)) upper bound that matches the lower bound.
impact: Provides a theoretically optimal, practical recipe for learning minimax policies in competitive multi‑agent and adversarial settings with limited (bandit) feedback—important where the final policy (not just the average) must perform well.
visual_elements: Log‑log plot of exploitability vs. iterations comparing: (a) this method showing slope −1/4, (b) prior algorithms with slower decay, and (c) the lower bound.
Flow diagram of the uncoupled bandit interaction: each player samples, receives bandit payoff, builds estimator, applies log‑barrier OMD update.
Illustration of the simplex with log‑barrier contours showing how the regularizer pushes iterates away from the boundary.
Compact algorithm box: pseudocode steps (sampling, estimator, update) with a badge showing the O(t^{-1/4)) guarantee.
paper_title: Optimal last-iterate convergence in matrix games with bandit feedback using the log-barrier
paper_authors: Come Fiegel, Pierre Menard, Tadashi Kozuno, Michal Valko, Vianney Perchet
